nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Dusk settles over Lanternvale like a warm quilt. Smoke curls from crooked chimneys, a windmill stands idle on the hill, and beneath the great camphor tree the spirit-lanterns glow the colour of honey.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Then, one by one, the flames under the tree shiver... shrink... and go out. The square falls silent. Somewhere a child starts to cry, and somewhere else a sheep joins in, out of solidarity.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Well. That's the great lantern gone, and the fourth this month. *An old woman with a long pipe peers at you through the smoke.* You've a traveller's dust on your boots. See anything grey on the road in?

choices.text: The spirits here are frightened. I can feel it, like a held breath.
That wasn't a fire going out. Something unmade it.
Something drank that light. I'd know the taste anywhere.
The birds went quiet a full minute before it happened.
The wind just stopped. The spirits of this place are holding very still.
Whatever is doing this, I'll stand against it.
Point me at whatever did it.
I saw nothing, I was nowhere, and I definitely didn't just pocket that candle stub.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Like ash that never knew a fire. We call it the Hollow. Where the lanterns go dark it creeps in, and whatever it touches forgets how to be itself.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Then you've the gift, and you're right. The little spirits of this valley sleep in the lantern-light. When it goes, so do they... and other things wake. We call it the Hollow.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Unmade. Yes. That's the word I've been hunting for all month. The thing that does the unmaking, we call the Hollow.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: ...Is that so. Then I'll trust your nose, and keep an eye on the rest of you. Whatever it is, we call it the Hollow.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Aye, they always know first. The wolves have been coming down out of Whisperwood too. Something's emptying the forest. We call it the Hollow.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Then the spirits are wiser than the rest of us, keeping still. Something is eating this valley's light. We call it the Hollow.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Bold. I like bold. Bold gets things done, and only occasionally gets eaten. What you'd be standing against, we call the Hollow.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Ha! If only it had a nose to punch. Perhaps it does. We call it the Hollow, and it's coming down from the mountain.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Keep the candle, dear. Light's in short supply. What you didn't see, we call the Hollow.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Every lantern in this valley is fed by the Heart Lantern at the Old Shrine, up past Whisperwood. If they're failing, something's wrong up there. I'm too old for the stair, and the village is too frightened to climb it.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: A warm bed at the Sleepy Lantern, a hot meal, the gratitude of a whole valley, and my second-best pipe. Also, if the lanterns fail, the Hollow won't stop at our borders. So: everything, really.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: So was everyone who ever lived here, once. Rest at the inn tonight. If you're still passing through in the morning, I'll not hold it against you. Much.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Good. Come and find me under Old Kusu once you've your bearings — the big tree, you can't miss it, it's been there four hundred years. And mind the dark.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: There you are! Can you hear it? The whole valley's humming. Tobben's weeping into his lamp-oil and pretending it's smoke. Thank you, truly.

choices.text: I have a letter for you, from Keeper Ishiro at the Old Shrine.
Keeper Ishiro is at peace now.
When the Heart Lantern flared, it showed me something. Ash, drifting down from the north.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: *The Elder's pipe goes still.* Ash. Then the Hollow did not grow here at all — it was carried, like a seed on the wind. If you mean to follow it, take the west road over Amberfield Downs to Brightwater. Archivist Penhallow keeps the old records there. If anyone knows what sleeps in the north, it is him.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: *She is quiet for a long moment.* Then he's finally on time for something. *She laughs, and wipes her eyes with the back of her pipe hand.* Thank you for telling me.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Bram's counting sheep and getting the same number twice running. The children have their spirit-friends back. And the windmill's turning again — Hollis cried. Don't tell him I told you.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Every lantern in the valley lit itself an hour ago. All at once. The whole village gasped like one big surprised cat. I take it that was you?

choices.text: The Warden is at peace, and the Heart Lantern burns again.
Seren performed the Kindling — with the light of every hearth in the valley, not her life.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Then the old stag walks again. Ha! You've given this valley back its light, and its children their spirit-friends. That's not a small thing. That's the only thing.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Not her life. *Her pipe trembles.* Oh, Isolde would have laughed and cried at once. Ten years I've kept that taper, waiting for someone stubborn enough to try it the other way.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Go on, then. The Sleepy Lantern's pouring for free tonight, and you're the reason. Dorrit will pretend it was her idea.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Ah, our traveller. Sit, sit — Old Kusu doesn't mind. If you're to help us, you'd best hear about the Warden.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Every autumn a great stag spirit walks down from the Old Shrine with lanterns hung in his antlers, and relights every lantern in the valley. We call him the Warden. This year he never came.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: And every ten years, a summoner climbs to the shrine to kindle the Heart Lantern anew. The last was Isolde. She lit it... and she never came down.

choices.text: Summoners who 'never come down'... The old Kindling asked for more than prayers, didn't it?
A spirit-flame needs something to burn. What did she give it?

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Nobody truly knows. Her guardian came back down alone and has scarcely said ten words since. He sits outside the inn most days in a red coat, watching the road.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Sharp. Yes. The old rite asks a summoner to give the Heart a piece of their own light. Most give a little. Isolde gave everything. That flame has kept us ten years, and now it's spent.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: *She squints at you.* You've read a book about it, haven't you? The wrong book. *She puffs her pipe and says no more about it.*

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Herself. A summoner gives the Heart Lantern a piece of their own spirit. Isolde gave all of hers, so the valley would have ten bright years. And it did.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: That's a question for a priest, dear, and you're asking an old woman with a pipe.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Take the pilgrim road east into Whisperwood. Halfway up there's a Wayside Shrine with its own little lantern spirit, Komorebi. If anyone knows what's gone wrong, she does. And take this.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: The Kindling Taper. Every hearth in Lanternvale gave it a spark the night Isolde climbed. It's never quite gone out. I've a feeling it wants to go home.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Buy potions from Tilly, eat Dorrit's stew, never trust a Mossling with anything shiny — and if you meet a grey thing that used to be something else, be kind if you can. They were ours, once.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Off you go. The lanterns won't wait, and neither will my pipe.

choices.text: I have a letter for you, from Keeper Ishiro at the Old Shrine.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Back already? The Hollow's still creeping, so I assume you're not finished.

choices.text: The Wayside spirit wants embers from the Hollow wisps.
The Wayside spirit wants embers from the Hollow wisps.
The Wayside spirit wants embers from the Hollow wisps.
Something called Rotheart seals the shrine stair.
What will I find at the shrine?
What will I find at the shrine?
The Heart Lantern needs a new flame.
I have a letter for you, from Keeper Ishiro at the Old Shrine.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: East through Bram's pasture, into Whisperwood, along the pilgrim road. The Wayside Shrine has a red gate, a little stone fox and a lantern that ought to be lit. You'll know it.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Embers from the wisps? Poor things. They were lantern-flames once, you know. Taking their light back isn't cruelty. It's a rescue.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Rotheart? He guarded the stair when I was a girl — a kind old tree who let children climb him. If he's gone grey... burn him clean, and don't let it break your heart.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: The sanctum's at the top of the stair. Keeper Ishiro tends it, though he's not written in months, and he used to write every week. Be careful up there.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Then light it. Whatever it costs. *She stops.* No. Not whatever it costs. We've paid that price before. Find a better way.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Still passing through, traveller? The lanterns aren't. They're going out, one by one.

choices.text: I'll help. Tell me what you need.
I have a letter for you, from Keeper Ishiro at the Old Shrine.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Anything else, dear? My pipe's going out, and that's one light I can fix myself.

choices.text: I have a letter for you, from Keeper Ishiro at the Old Shrine.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: It isn't a creature. It's an absence — the shape a light leaves behind when it's taken. Beasts it touches go grey and angry. Spirits it touches forget their own names.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: A stag as tall as the inn, made of mist and moss, with a hundred lanterns in his antlers. When I was small I left honey cakes out for him on Walk Night. He always ate them. Spirits are terribly greedy about honey.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: Old Kusu was here before the village. The first lamplighters tied the shimenawa rope round him and asked his leave to settle. He said yes, or at least he didn't say no, which with trees is much the same.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: *She breaks the grey wax and reads aloud, quietly.* 'Maru. The Warden came to the Heart tonight and did not light his antlers. He drank from it instead. I am afraid. Send someone.' ...Three weeks ago. Oh, Ishiro.

nodes.speaker: elder_maru
nodes.text: If you meet him up there, tell him it arrived. Tell him I'm sorry it was late. He'll understand — he was never on time for anything in his life.

nodes.speaker: innkeeper_dorrit
nodes.text: The hero of the hour! Sit down, sit down — tonight it's on the house, and I'll hear no argument. There'll be singing later, I'm afraid. Hollis has been practising.

choices.text: I'd like a room for the night.
Who's the man in the red coat outside?
Any chance of a discount for a hero-in-training?

nodes.speaker: innkeeper_dorrit
nodes.text: Welcome to the Sleepy Lantern! Mind the cat, mind the step, mind your head on the beam. Hungry? Tired? Both? It's usually both.

choices.text: I'd like a room for the night.
Who's the man in the red coat outside?
Any chance of a discount for a hero-in-training?

nodes.speaker: innkeeper_dorrit
nodes.text: Anything else, love?

choices.text: I'd like a room for the night.
Who's the man in the red coat outside?
Any chance of a discount for a hero-in-training?

nodes.speaker: innkeeper_dorrit
nodes.text: Top of the stairs, second door. The beds are feather, the quilts are patchwork, and the floorboard by the window sings. Sweet dreams.

nodes.speaker: innkeeper_dorrit
nodes.text: Bram's lost three ewes to wolves this week. Old Tobben swears Mosslings are nicking his wicks. And poor Fennick came back from Whisperwood without his mailbag, white as milk. Something about spiders.

nodes.speaker: innkeeper_dorrit
nodes.text: Oh, and Sergeant Holt's in a state about bandits at the Old Bridge. And little Nell's lost her spirit-friend. Busy month for bad news, and it's not even harvest.

nodes.speaker: innkeeper_dorrit
nodes.text: Kael? Pays for a week at a time, drinks one cup of tea a day, and watches the road. Ten years now. He's not unkind, love. He's just... waiting.

nodes.speaker: innkeeper_dorrit
nodes.text: Ha! Cheeky. I like cheeky. Here — two bowls of stew on the house, and don't tell the cat, he'll want one.

nodes.speaker: innkeeper_dorrit
nodes.text: Nice try, love. Prices are prices. The cat, however, accepts compliments free of charge.

nodes.speaker: merchant_tilly
nodes.text: Business is booming! Everyone wants lantern oil for the festival. I'm calling it 'Festival Oil' now. It's the same oil. Don't tell anyone.

choices.text: Your scales are off. Only slightly — and in your favour.

nodes.speaker: merchant_tilly
nodes.text: Tilly Brambleback's General Goods! Potions, pickles, lantern oil and wands. The wands are new. The pickles are not.

choices.text: Your scales are off. Only slightly — and in your favour.

nodes.speaker: merchant_tilly
nodes.text: What else can I tempt you with?

choices.text: Your scales are off. Only slightly — and in your favour.

nodes.speaker: merchant_tilly
nodes.text: My Lantern-Oil Tonic! Lamp oil, honey, camphor and a great deal of hope. Keeps the grey off you — I've seen it work. Mostly I've seen people feel better, which counts.

nodes.speaker: merchant_tilly
nodes.text: ...Oh, stars. Twenty years I've had those scales. *She presses a few bottles into your hands.* Take these, and please don't mention it to Sergeant Holt.

nodes.speaker: merchant_tilly
nodes.text: *She follows your gaze to the scales.* Those are antiques, dear. Antiques are allowed to be eccentric.

nodes.speaker: smith_garrow
nodes.text: *CLANG.* Garrow Ironhand, weaponsmith. Swords, axes, maces, bows — if it's pointy, heavy, or pointy AND heavy, I've got it.

choices.text: Need a hand with that anvil?
You and the armorer look alike.

nodes.speaker: smith_garrow
nodes.text: *He wipes his hands on his apron.* What else?

choices.text: Need a hand with that anvil?
You and the armorer look alike.

nodes.speaker: smith_garrow
nodes.text: Hah! You lifted the whole thing! Bess owes me a silver. Here — take some whetstones. They like a strong arm.

nodes.speaker: smith_garrow
nodes.text: *You heave. The anvil does not.* It likes you, it's just not ready to move in together. Takes a while, with anvils.

nodes.speaker: smith_garrow
nodes.text: Bess? My sister. She does armour, I do weapons, we both do arguing. You'll need both from us, so we've agreed to be civil in front of customers.

nodes.speaker: smith_garrow
nodes.text: Can't sleep. Every time a lantern goes out I hear it, like a bell that stops ringing. So I hit metal until I can't hear it any more.

nodes.speaker: armorer_bess
nodes.text: Bess Ironhand, armorer. Cloth, leather, mail and plate — and before you ask, yes, the plate's real, and no, you probably can't wear it yet.

choices.text: Why couldn't I wear the plate?

nodes.speaker: armorer_bess
nodes.text: Anything else? I've got buckles to polish.

choices.text: Why couldn't I wear the plate?

nodes.speaker: armorer_bess
nodes.text: Plate's a craft, not a coat. Takes years of drill to move in it without falling over. Come back when you've the scars for it — or buy it now and hang it on the wall. I'm not fussy.

nodes.speaker: armorer_bess
nodes.text: ...He's been forging all night since the lanterns started going out. Says it keeps his hands busy. Tell him to sleep, if he'll listen to anyone.

nodes.speaker: armorer_bess
nodes.text: I'm worried about my prices, she says briskly, and nothing more.

nodes.speaker: trainer_odo
nodes.text: Ha! The lanterns are lit and my knees have stopped aching. Coincidence? I think not. What'll it be?

choices.text: Teach me something that hits harder.
I want to unlearn my talents.
You hold your sword like a man who lost someone to it.
Could I practise on that training dummy?

nodes.speaker: trainer_odo
nodes.text: Sir Odo Brightwater — retired, unretired, and retired again. I train warriors and paladins: the shouty sort and the shiny sort.

choices.text: Teach me something that hits harder.
I want to unlearn my talents.
You hold your sword like a man who lost someone to it.
Could I practise on that training dummy?

nodes.speaker: trainer_odo
nodes.text: Anything else?

choices.text: Teach me something that hits harder.
I want to unlearn my talents.
You hold your sword like a man who lost someone to it.
Could I practise on that training dummy?

nodes.speaker: trainer_odo
nodes.text: Harder! Splendid. Stance, breath, follow-through. The shouting comes naturally.

nodes.speaker: trainer_odo
nodes.text: Then let's see how brightly you burn. Seals first, judgement after, humility always.

nodes.speaker: trainer_odo
nodes.text: Unlearning is harder than learning, and costs more besides. Shall we begin?

nodes.speaker: trainer_odo
nodes.text: *Odo's smile fades.* My squire. Forty years ago, on the pilgrim stair. *He straightens.* Which is why I teach you lot to come home. Again.

nodes.speaker: trainer_odo
nodes.text: Odo laughs. 'I hold it like a man with a bad shoulder, friend.'

nodes.speaker: trainer_odo
nodes.text: Sir Turnip? By all means. He's never once hit back, which is more than I can say for my students. Mind his nose.

nodes.speaker: trainer_fennel
nodes.text: Hear that? Birdsong. Proper, silly, morning birdsong. I'd forgotten how loud it is. Training?

choices.text: I need to sharpen my aim.
I want to unlearn my talents.
The pasture grass is greying at the tips. Is the Hollow in the soil?

nodes.speaker: trainer_fennel
nodes.text: Fennel Greythorn. I teach hunters to listen to the wild, and shamans to listen to the spirits under it. Most folk can't tell the difference. The wolves can.

choices.text: I need to sharpen my aim.
I want to unlearn my talents.
The pasture grass is greying at the tips. Is the Hollow in the soil?

nodes.speaker: trainer_fennel
nodes.text: Anything else?

choices.text: I need to sharpen my aim.
I want to unlearn my talents.
The pasture grass is greying at the tips. Is the Hollow in the soil?

nodes.speaker: trainer_fennel
nodes.text: Breathe out, loose on the empty. And feed your pet first. Always first.

nodes.speaker: trainer_fennel
nodes.text: They are. The Hollow's made them jumpy. Let me show you how to calm them — and how to point them.

nodes.speaker: trainer_fennel
nodes.text: Unlearning is harder than learning, and costs more besides. Shall we begin?

nodes.speaker: trainer_fennel
nodes.text: ...Good eye. Not in the soil — in the light. Plants are just the first to notice. Take this; it's more use to you than me.

nodes.speaker: trainer_fennel
nodes.text: 'Could be drought,' Fennel says, very unconvinced.

nodes.speaker: trainer_quillon
nodes.text: The floating books have started humming. I think they're happy. Or hungry. What do you need?

choices.text: I'm ready for more advanced spells.
I want to unlearn my talents.
The lantern-flames run on spirit, not oil. That's why the Hollow can eat them.

nodes.speaker: trainer_quillon
nodes.text: Magister Quillon Ashby. Do not touch the floating books, do not feed the floating books, and do not, under any circumstances, read the floating books aloud.

choices.text: I'm ready for more advanced spells.
I want to unlearn my talents.
The lantern-flames run on spirit, not oil. That's why the Hollow can eat them.

nodes.speaker: trainer_quillon
nodes.text: Anything else?

choices.text: I'm ready for more advanced spells.
I want to unlearn my talents.
The lantern-flames run on spirit, not oil. That's why the Hollow can eat them.

nodes.speaker: trainer_quillon
nodes.text: Ah, a scholar! Fireball? Frostbolt? Something tasteful in arcane? Sit. Don't touch anything.

nodes.speaker: trainer_quillon
nodes.text: Of course you do. I teach it under protest, with the windows open.

nodes.speaker: trainer_quillon
nodes.text: Unlearning is harder than learning, and costs more besides. Shall we begin?

nodes.speaker: trainer_quillon
nodes.text: Exactly! At last, someone who reads! Here — some of my study scrolls. Don't let them get damp. They sulk.

nodes.speaker: trainer_quillon
nodes.text: 'Close,' he says, in the tone of a man who means 'not remotely'.

nodes.speaker: trainer_wick
nodes.text: The shrine bell rang on its own last night. Nobody touched it. I choose to believe it was saying thank you.

choices.text: I would learn more of the Light.
I want to unlearn my talents.

nodes.speaker: trainer_wick
nodes.text: Brother Wick. I tend the village shrine, and in the evenings I teach... other skills. I was a cutpurse once, before the lanterns caught me. Light and shadow, friend. You can't have one without the other.

choices.text: I would learn more of the Light.
I want to unlearn my talents.

nodes.speaker: trainer_wick
nodes.text: Anything else?

choices.text: I would learn more of the Light.
I want to unlearn my talents.

nodes.speaker: trainer_wick
nodes.text: Then pray with your hands as well as your heart. Healing is work, not wishing.

nodes.speaker: trainer_wick
nodes.text: Quieter, quicker, kinder when it counts. Let's begin.

nodes.speaker: trainer_wick
nodes.text: Unlearning is harder than learning, and costs more besides. Shall we begin?

nodes.speaker: trainer_wick
nodes.text: You lift a little purse. He doesn't notice — then grins and pats the empty pocket. 'Good! Keep it. Consider it tuition, refunded.'

nodes.speaker: trainer_wick
nodes.text: *His hand closes, very gently, over yours.* 'Ah. Not yet. But your heart was in it.'

nodes.speaker: guard_holt
nodes.text: Bridge is quiet, traders are moving and nobody's been stabbed all week. I could get used to this.

nodes.speaker: guard_holt
nodes.text: Mending fences in the east field, singing badly. Strangest thing I've seen in twenty years of guarding, and I once saw a goose run for council.

nodes.speaker: guard_holt
nodes.text: Well? Is the bridge clear?

choices.text: They were farmers. Their fields went grey, so they took the bridge. I sent them here for honest work.
They won't be back. I made sure of it.
I paid them to leave the valley.
The bandits won't trouble anyone again.

nodes.speaker: guard_holt
nodes.text: ...Farmers. Of course they were. Right. Dorrit needs hands and the mill needs a strong back. I'll find them work. You did a kinder thing than I asked, friend.

nodes.speaker: guard_holt
nodes.text: Good. Can't say I'll miss them. Can't say I'd want to live in the next valley over, either.

nodes.speaker: guard_holt
nodes.text: You... paid them. With money. *He rubs his face.* Well, it worked, and nobody's bleeding. I'll put it in the report as 'diplomacy'.

nodes.speaker: guard_holt
nodes.text: Hm. Not how I'd have liked it, but it's done. The road's yours to walk again — yours, and every pilgrim's.

nodes.speaker: guard_holt
nodes.text: Here. The valley's thanks, such as the guard budget allows. Which is not very much.

nodes.speaker: guard_holt
nodes.text: The Old Bridge, friend. Past the Wayside Shrine. Bandits, tolls, unhappy pilgrims. You know the one.

nodes.speaker: guard_holt
nodes.text: Sergeant Holt, Lanternvale Guard. All of it — I'm the whole guard. What can I do for you?

choices.text: About the bandits at the Old Bridge — it's already handled.
You're more worried than you're letting on.

nodes.speaker: guard_holt
nodes.text: Bandits at the Old Bridge in Whisperwood, charging 'tolls' to anyone on the pilgrim road. Usually that means a stabbing, eventually. I can't leave the village. You could.

nodes.speaker: guard_holt
nodes.text: Run them off however you like. I'd prefer the kind of 'however' that doesn't end with you dead. Good luck.

nodes.speaker: guard_holt
nodes.text: *He lowers his voice.* Bandits I can handle. It's the grey that frightens me. You can't arrest a colour.

nodes.speaker: guard_holt
nodes.text: Worried? I'm a guard. Worry's the uniform.

nodes.speaker: shepherd_bram
nodes.text: The flock's sleeping easy, and so am I, first time in weeks. If you ever want a lamb named after you, just say the word.

nodes.speaker: shepherd_bram
nodes.text: Is it done? Is he...?

choices.text: Greymane won't trouble your flock again.

nodes.speaker: shepherd_bram
nodes.text: Poor old devil. He kept this valley's wolves honest for ten years, you know. It's not his fault the grey got him. *He sniffs.* Thank you. Truly.

nodes.speaker: shepherd_bram
nodes.text: Take something for your trouble. Not a sheep. Something else.

nodes.speaker: shepherd_bram
nodes.text: His den's just inside Whisperwood, under the big rocks back from the road. You'll smell it before you see it. Mind yourself — he's not called the old alpha for nothing.

nodes.speaker: shepherd_bram
nodes.text: You chased 'em off? All three? Bless you. But they'll be back. They're not hungry, see — they're scared. Running from something in the woods.

choices.text: Let me look at those tracks again.
Wolves only run from bigger wolves.

nodes.speaker: shepherd_bram
nodes.text: *You kneel. The prints are panicked, wide-spaced — and one set is huge, with a grey crust in each print like frost that never melts.* 'Greymane,' Bram whispers. 'The old alpha.' He presses a potion into your hand.

nodes.speaker: shepherd_bram
nodes.text: Mud, mostly. And sheep. Bram looks hopeful, then less hopeful.

nodes.speaker: shepherd_bram
nodes.text: There's an old alpha, Greymane, dens at the edge of Whisperwood. If he's gone grey like the rest, the pack'll follow him anywhere. Would you...? He was a good wolf, once. Put him to rest.

nodes.speaker: shepherd_bram
nodes.text: They come at dusk into the far corner of the east pasture. Three of 'em, I think — though they look like thirty when you're one man with a crook.

nodes.speaker: shepherd_bram
nodes.text: Oh! Hello. Sorry. Counting. Thirty-one sheep. Thirty. ...Thirty.

choices.text: That ewe's limping. Let me take a look.

nodes.speaker: shepherd_bram
nodes.text: Wolves. They've been at the flock every night since the lanterns started failing. Lost three ewes already. I'm a shepherd, not a fighter. Would you see them off?

nodes.speaker: shepherd_bram
nodes.text: Bless you. They gather in the far corner of the pasture, by the hay. Mind the gate — Daisy bites.

nodes.speaker: shepherd_bram
nodes.text: *You tease a thorn out of her hoof. She headbutts you, affectionately. Bram beams like a proud father.*

nodes.speaker: shepherd_bram
nodes.text: *She headbutts you. Not affectionately.*

nodes.speaker: child_nell
nodes.text: Moppet says thank you! He says it in jingles. That one meant 'thank you'. That one meant 'cake'.

nodes.speaker: child_nell
nodes.text: Did you— is he— MOPPET!

choices.text: He was hiding under the glowing mushrooms. He's safe.

nodes.speaker: child_nell
nodes.text: *A tiny spirit tumbles into Nell's arms with a jingle.* He was scared of the dark, he says. I told him I'm not scared of anything. ...I was a bit scared. This is my luckiest thing. You have it. You need it more.

nodes.speaker: child_nell
nodes.text: And if you ever get scared, ring a bell. Somebody always comes.

nodes.speaker: child_nell
nodes.text: Ring my bell where it's quiet, and he'll come. He likes mushrooms that glow and places where grown-ups never look. And honey cake. He REALLY likes honey cake.

nodes.speaker: child_nell
nodes.text: Have you seen Moppet? He's small and green-ish and he's got a leaf on his head and he jingles. He ran away when the big lantern went out.

nodes.speaker: child_nell
nodes.text: My spirit friend! Nearly every kid in Lanternvale has one. They live in the lantern-light. When it went dark he got scared and ran to the woods. I'm not allowed in the woods.

nodes.speaker: child_nell
nodes.text: ...A bit. Don't tell Toby.

nodes.speaker: child_nell
nodes.text: I'm not scared of ANYTHING, says Nell, very loudly.

nodes.speaker: child_nell
nodes.text: Take my bell. Ring it where it's quiet, and he'll know you're my friend. Please find him?

nodes.speaker: child_nell
nodes.text: Thank you thank you THANK you. He likes honey cake, if you need to bribe him. I always need to bribe him.

nodes.speaker: lamplighter_tobben
nodes.text: I hung a lantern at the edge of Whisperwood, for the little thieves. Every morning there's a mushroom left on the post. Every morning I eat it. We've an understanding.

nodes.speaker: lamplighter_tobben
nodes.text: Every wick back in its lantern. Not that it matters while the Heart's dark... but it will matter, once it's lit. It will.

nodes.speaker: lamplighter_tobben
nodes.text: Did you find them? My wicks?

choices.text: The Mosslings gave them back. They only took them to light a lantern of their own — they're scared of the Hollow too.

nodes.speaker: lamplighter_tobben
nodes.text: ...A lantern of their own. Forty years I've shooed them off my stores, and they only wanted the same as the rest of us. I'll hang one for them at the forest edge. Light's for everyone.

nodes.speaker: lamplighter_tobben
nodes.text: Slightly nibbled! They nibble everything. Thank you — I'll have these trimmed and back in their lanterns by nightfall.

nodes.speaker: lamplighter_tobben
nodes.text: Here. Lamplighter's wages, and a lamplighter's thanks.

nodes.speaker: lamplighter_tobben
nodes.text: Little muddy leaf-shaped footprints, all over my stores. Mosslings! They camp just east of the Wayside Shrine. Six wicks, that's all I need. Don't let them talk you into a trade. They always win the trade.

nodes.speaker: lamplighter_tobben
nodes.text: Ah! Mind the ladder. Forty years I've lit these lanterns, and I've never seen them go out on their own. Now they won't relight. And someone's been stealing my wicks besides.

nodes.speaker: lamplighter_tobben
nodes.text: Spirit-wicks — braided under the full moon, blessed at the shrine. The Mosslings have been pinching them. Fetch me back six and I'll make it worth your while.

nodes.speaker: lamplighter_tobben
nodes.text: Bless you. Their camp's in Whisperwood, just past the Wayside Shrine. Look for tiny tents and a lot of very guilty faces.

nodes.speaker: lamplighter_tobben
nodes.text: *You realise:* the flame isn't fire, it's spirit — it has to come down from the Heart Lantern. Tobben stares. 'Forty years, and nobody ever explained it that neatly.'

nodes.speaker: lamplighter_tobben
nodes.text: 'Damp?' you suggest. Tobben gives you a look that has outlasted forty winters.

nodes.speaker: postman_fennick
nodes.text: Every letter delivered! Well. Nearly every letter. One was addressed to 'the moon'. I'm still working on that one.

nodes.speaker: postman_fennick
nodes.text: Did the Elder get Ishiro's letter? I keep thinking... if I'd not dropped it...

choices.text: I'm taking it to her now.

nodes.speaker: postman_fennick
nodes.text: That's— that's MY SATCHEL!

nodes.speaker: postman_fennick
nodes.text: My satchel! You found my satchel! Oh, it's sticky. Why is it sticky? No — don't tell me.

choices.text: (Slip a letter out to read before you hand it over.)

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: You palm a letter sealed with grey wax: 'To Elder Maru, from the Old Shrine. URGENT.' The handwriting shakes. You slide it back before Fennick notices.

nodes.speaker: postman_fennick
nodes.text: Ah-ah! *He catches your wrist.* Lanternvale Post. Sacred trust. *He looks more hurt than angry.*

nodes.speaker: postman_fennick
nodes.text: *He sorts the letters with shaking hands.* Seed catalogue, seed catalogue, love letter — not mine, sadly — and... oh no. This one's from the Old Shrine. Keeper Ishiro, to the Elder. It's three weeks late.

nodes.speaker: postman_fennick
nodes.text: I can't bring it to her. Three weeks late, from the shrine, with the lanterns failing? She'll look at me and I'll know. ...Would you take it? Please?

choices.text: It isn't your fault, Fennick. A spider took it, not you.

nodes.speaker: postman_fennick
nodes.text: *He laughs, a bit wetly.* Spiders. Of all the things. *He straightens his cap.* You're right. I'll come by later and tell her myself. But you go first. Please.

nodes.speaker: postman_fennick
nodes.text: *He only shakes his head and presses the letter into your hands.*

nodes.speaker: postman_fennick
nodes.text: Thank you. Under Old Kusu, she'll be — she always is, this time of day.

nodes.speaker: postman_fennick
nodes.text: And... sorry. To her. From me.

nodes.speaker: postman_fennick
nodes.text: It's in the spiders' hollow, east of the Old Bridge. I heard it go. Rustle-rustle-drag. I'll hear it in my sleep.

nodes.speaker: postman_fennick
nodes.text: Fennick, Royal Lanternvale Post! Well. Lanternvale Post. Well. Me.

nodes.speaker: postman_fennick
nodes.text: A boar charged me on the Whisperwood road! I dropped the satchel and ran, and when I looked back — spiders. Big ones. They dragged it off to their hollow. Every letter in the valley, in a spider's larder.

nodes.speaker: postman_fennick
nodes.text: Oh, thank you! If they've eaten the seed catalogues, don't tell Bram. He's been waiting for the turnips.

nodes.speaker: villager_june
nodes.text: The marigolds are blooming twice over! I'm putting them on every lantern in the valley. Twice.

nodes.speaker: villager_june
nodes.text: Marigolds for the lanterns? They like marigolds best. Don't ask me how I know. ...I talk to them.

choices.text: Your flowers are wilting at the edges.

nodes.speaker: villager_june
nodes.text: Not in words. In warmth. Lately they've gone so quiet I keep checking they're still there.

nodes.speaker: villager_june
nodes.text: *She looks closer.* Grey at the tips... You're right. The Hollow's in the meadow now. *She tucks a marigold into your collar.* For luck. Keep it in your heart, if not in water.

nodes.speaker: villager_june
nodes.text: They're just tired, June says, hugging her basket a little tighter.

nodes.speaker: villager_hollis
nodes.text: Hear that creaking? She's turning! First wind in a month, the moment the lanterns lit. Flour for the festival cakes! I may cry. I may already be crying.

nodes.speaker: villager_hollis
nodes.text: The windmill only turns when the lanterns are lit. Daft, isn't it? But it's true. No wind since the great lantern went out — the sails just hang there.

choices.text: Why would a windmill need lanterns?

nodes.speaker: villager_hollis
nodes.text: Because the wind in this valley's a spirit, same as everything else here. Ask Fennel, she'll explain it better. And longer. Much longer.

nodes.speaker: child_toby
nodes.text: I'm a knight! This is my sword. Its name is Stick.

choices.text: A fine name for a sword.
Kneel, Toby. I dub thee Knight of the Well.

nodes.speaker: child_toby
nodes.text: It's a FIERCE name. Stick has slain eleven dragons. They were mostly dandelions. One was a cabbage.

nodes.speaker: child_toby
nodes.text: *Toby kneels so fast he falls over.* I'M A REAL KNIGHT, *he informs the entire village.* STICK, WE'RE REAL.

nodes.speaker: child_toby
nodes.text: She lost Moppet. She says she's not sad but she is. I gave her my best beetle and she's still sad. That was my BEST beetle.

nodes.speaker: rusk
nodes.text: Honest work. Feels strange. Good strange.

choices.text: You still owe me a toll refund.

nodes.speaker: rusk
nodes.text: Dorrit feeds us till we can't move, and Hollis says my back's worth two mules. Once the lanterns are lit, Stoneford's fields'll come back. We'll go home in spring.

nodes.speaker: rusk
nodes.text: Ha! *He digs in his coat.* Here. The last coin I didn't spend on seed. Kept it for luck. Reckon you're luckier than me. Plant something with it.
